mainTopic: Who the waters check besides the סוטה, how רבי עקיבא and רבי learn it from the פסוקים, and the lessons of the repeated "נטמאה", ending with a קל וחומר from סוטה to ספק טומאה.
overview: The amud opens by finishing the question of who "אוֹתוֹ" (him) is in the משנה. It cannot be the בעל, since the waters do not work at all if the husband has sinned. So it must be the בועל, and the different wording in the סיפא is just style. Next the גמרא asks how רבי עקיבא's proof "ובאו ובאו" reads, and proves from רבי's opposing view that רבי עקיבא learns from the extra letter ו. So for רבי עקיבא there are six lessons, three for the woman and three for the man, while רבי has only three. רבי gets the rule that the waters check the man from "לצבות בטן ולנפל ירך". רבי עקיבא uses that same phrase to teach that the כהן tells her the belly is struck before the thigh. Finally, a ברייתא counts three mentions of "נטמאה": for the husband, the paramour, and תרומה. רבי ישמעאל forbids her to a כהן by a קל וחומר. The ברייתא then learns that a ספק סוטה is forbidden and starts a קל וחומר from סוטה to ספק טומאת שרץ, which finishes on the next amud.

steps.title: Rejecting the idea that 'him' means the husband
steps.stepSummary: If "אוֹתוֹ" meant that the waters check the בעל for his own sin, that cannot be right. When the husband has sinned, the waters do not check the wife at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: Suppose 'him' means the husband: if he has a sin, the water checks him. But when he himself has a sin, does the water even check her?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a question from the previous daf. It is testing whether "him" in the משנה could mean the husband, and it pushes back on that idea.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The suggestion was that the waters check the husband too, catching him if he has sinned in a similar way. The גמרא answers that this makes no sense: if the husband has sinned, the waters will not work on the wife either. So there is no situation where they test both of them together.

keyTerms.meaning: A sin; here, forbidden relations like the sin the wife is suspected of
The water checks / tests (the bitter waters of the סוטה)
In himself, his own
Does it really…? (opens a doubting question)

phrases.english: that if he has an iniquity
phrases.notes: This continues a question from the end of the previous daf: maybe 'him' in the משנה means the husband.

phrases.english: the water checks him,
when he himself has an iniquity,
does the water check her at all?

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי אִית בֵּיהּ עָוֹן בְּדִידֵיהּ מִי בָּדְקִי לַהּ מַיָּא לְדִידַהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the question begun on the previous daf about who 'אוֹתוֹ' refers to.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading that 'אוֹתוֹ' in the משנה refers to the husband.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the husband has sinned, the waters do not test the wife at all, so they cannot test both of them together.

steps.title: A ברייתא: the waters work only when the husband is clean
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא reads the פסוק "ונקה האיש מעון" to mean that the waters check the wife only when the husband is free of sin.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא teaches on the verse 'And the man shall be clear of sin, and that woman shall bear her sin': when the man is clean of sin, the water checks his wife. When he is not clean of sin, the water does not check his wife.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a source to back up its challenge in step 1. A ברייתא shows that a sinning husband cancels the test.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא reads the פסוק as a condition. Only if the man is 'clear of sin' will the woman 'bear her sin' through the waters. This makes the husband reading of 'him' impossible, so the גמרא has to look for someone else.

keyTerms.meaning: But isn't it taught (in a ברייתא)? This brings a source against the idea
And the man shall be clear of sin (במדבר 5:31)
Clean, free (of sin)

steps.whatToRemember: The waters of the סוטה only work if the husband himself is free of sin. So "him" in the משנה cannot mean the husband.

phrases.english: But isn't it taught in a baraita:
'And the man shall be clear from iniquity
phrases.notes: במדבר 5:31

phrases.english: and that woman shall bear her iniquity.'
When the man is clear of iniquity,
the water checks his wife;
if the man is not clear of iniquity,
the water does not check his wife!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source that backs up the challenge in step 1.
steps.raayaObject: That 'him' cannot mean the husband, since the waters do not work when the husband has sinned.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא reading of במדבר 5:31, 'ונקה האיש מעון'.

steps.title: If it means the paramour, why not say so like the סיפא does?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא now tries "him" as the בועל. It challenges this: the סיפא names the בועל openly, so the רישא should name him too.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, 'him' means the paramour. But then let the משנה say it the way the later clause does: 'Just as she is forbidden to the husband, so she is forbidden to the paramour!'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא switches to the second option, that 'him' is the paramour. Right away it raises a problem with the משנה's wording.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the סיפא, the משנה clearly writes 'לבועל.' If the רישא also means the בועל, it should have written his name, and not just the vague word 'him.' The different wording seems to hint that the רישא is talking about someone else.

keyTerms.meaning: The paramour, the man suspected with the wife
Let it teach / it should have said
The later clause of the משנה
Forbidden

phrases.english: But rather, it refers to the paramour —
then let it teach as the latter clause teaches:
Just as she is forbidden to the husband,
so she is forbidden to the paramour!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the husband reading fails, the גמרא tries the paramour reading and challenges it.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading that 'אוֹתוֹ' in the רישא refers to the בועל.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The סיפא names the בועל openly. If the רישא meant him too, it should have done the same and not used the vague word 'him'.

steps.title: Yes, it is the paramour; the wording just matches its neighbor
steps.stepSummary: "Him" really is the בועל. The רישא said "אוֹתוֹ" to match "אוֹתָהּ", and the סיפא said "בועל" to match "בעל".
steps.simpleTranslation: Really it means the paramour. In the first clause, since it said 'her,' it said 'him.' In the later clause, since it said 'husband,' it said 'paramour.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge from step 3. The paramour reading stands, and the change in wording is just style.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה picks its words to sound parallel inside each clause. In the רישא, the word next to it was 'her,' so the matching word is 'him.' In the סיפא, the word next to it was 'husband,' so the matching word is 'paramour.' Both clauses mean the same person.

keyTerms.meaning: Really / in fact (keeps the original idea)
Since it taught (one word, it taught the matching word)
The first clause of the משנה

steps.whatToRemember: In the משנה, "אוֹתוֹ" means the בועל. The waters check the paramour just as they check the wife.

phrases.english: Really it refers to the paramour,
and in the first clause, since it taught 'her,'
it taught 'him.'
In the latter clause, since it taught 'husband,'
it taught 'paramour.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 3.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Stylistic explanation of the משנה's wording
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The different wording in the רישא ('him') and the סיפא ('paramour') suggests they refer to different people.
steps.terutzMaskana: Both clauses mean the בועל. Each clause just matches the word right next to it: 'her' goes with 'him', and 'husband' goes with 'paramour'.

steps.title: How exactly does the משנה read the proof 'and shall enter'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's proof "ובאו ובאו" and asks which version is correct. Is it "באו" then "ובאו", or "ובאו" twice?
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'As it says: "and shall enter," "and shall enter."' A question was asked: does it say 'shall enter' and then 'and shall enter,' or 'and shall enter' and 'and shall enter'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves on to the next line of the משנה, the proof that the waters check the paramour. It asks how the משנה's words should read, which sets up a discussion of where the proof comes from.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the text is 'באו, ובאו,' the proof comes from the extra letter ו added to the word. If the text is 'ובאו, ובאו,' the proof comes from the same phrase showing up twice in two פסוקים. The question is about which of these two ways the proof works.

keyTerms.meaning: As it is said (bringing a פסוק as a source)
And they (the waters) shall enter
A question was asked of them (step 8 answers it)
Is it saying

steps.confusionAlert: This is not an argument about the הלכה. Everyone agrees the waters check the בועל. The question is only how the משנה's text reads, and so which detail in the פסוקים the proof is built on.

phrases.english: 'As it says: "and shall enter," "and shall enter."'
phrases.notes: The גמרא is quoting the משנה's proof here. The פסוקים are במדבר 5:24 and 5:27.

phrases.english: A question was asked of them:
Does it say 'shall enter,' 'and shall enter,'
or does it say 'and shall enter,' 'and shall enter'?
phrases.notes: The difference is whether the proof comes from the extra letter ו, or from the phrase being written twice.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to the next line of the משנה, the scriptural proof for checking the בועל.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the משנה reads 'באו ובאו', with the proof from the extra ו, or 'ובאו ובאו', with the proof from the phrase repeating in two פסוקים.

steps.title: A proof attempt from רבי עקיבא's parallel teaching about 'is defiled'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא tries to settle the question by pointing to רבי עקיבא's other teaching in the משנה. That teaching is built the same way, on 'נטמאה' and 'ונטמאה'.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: just as she is forbidden to her husband, so she is forbidden to the man she was with, as it says 'is defiled' and 'and is defiled'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings רבי עקיבא's second teaching in the משנה to help answer the question from step 5.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this teaching, רבי עקיבא forbids the wife to both the בעל and the בועל. His proof is written 'נטמאה' and then 'ונטמאה'. The idea is that his first teaching ('באו ובאו') should be read the same way.

keyTerms.meaning: She is forbidden
The man the wife was secluded with
She became defiled (impure)

phrases.english: Come and hear:
Just as she is forbidden to the husband
so she is forbidden to the paramour,
as it is said: "is defiled," "and is defiled."
phrases.notes: במדבר 5:29. This is רבי עקיבא's second teaching in the משנה.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע: כְּשֵׁם שֶׁאֲסוּרָה לַבַּעַל כָּךְ אֲסוּרָה לַבּוֹעֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tries to answer the question about the wording that was raised in step 5.
steps.raayaObject: Which wording is correct in רבי עקיבא's teaching of 'באו ובאו'.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי עקיבא's parallel teaching in the משנה, 'נטמאה ונטמאה'.

steps.title: The parallel teaching has the same doubt
steps.stepSummary: The proof does not work. We could ask the very same question about 'נטמאה ונטמאה'.
steps.simpleTranslation: But you can still ask: does he say 'is defiled, is defiled', or does he say 'is defiled, and is defiled'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the proof. The parallel teaching is just as unclear as the first one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Maybe רבי עקיבא is learning from the fact that the word 'נטמאה' shows up twice in the פרשה. Or maybe he is learning from the extra ו in 'ונטמאה'. Since we cannot tell which, this teaching cannot settle the first question.

keyTerms.meaning: But still
Let it be asked; the doubt remains
Is he saying

phrases.english: But still, let it be asked:
Is he saying "is defiled," "is defiled,"
phrases.notes: Meaning: he learns from the word being repeated in two different פסוקים.

phrases.english: or is he saying "is defiled," "and is defiled"?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof from step 6.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The whole proof from the parallel teaching.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The parallel teaching is unclear in exactly the same way, so it cannot settle the question.

steps.title: Proof from רבי's dispute: רבי עקיבא learns from the ו's
steps.stepSummary: רבי learns the two prohibitions from the two times 'ונטמאה' appears in the פרשה. Since he disagrees with רבי עקיבא, רבי עקיבא must be learning from the extra ו.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear from the סיפא: רבי says, the two times 'and is defiled' is said in the פרשה are one for the husband and one for the paramour. This shows that רבי עקיבא learns from the ו's.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a real proof from the end of the משנה. רבי's opinion there shows us how רבי עקיבא learns.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי gets his two rules from the word appearing twice in the פרשה. רבי is arguing with רבי עקיבא, so רבי עקיבא's source must be something different. That source is the extra letter ו. This answers the question from step 5.

keyTerms.meaning: The later part of the משנה
By inference; we can tell from this
He learns from the extra letters ו

steps.whatToRemember: רבי learns from a word being repeated in the פרשה. רבי עקיבא learns from the extra ו at the start of a word.
steps.confusionAlert: Both רבי and רבי עקיבא reach the same rule here: she is forbidden to both the בעל and the בועל. They only argue about which part of the פסוק teaches it.

phrases.english: Come and hear from what is taught in the latter clause,
Rabbi says:
the two times that are said in the passage
"and is defiled," "and is defiled":
phrases.notes: במדבר 5:14 and 5:29

phrases.english: one for the husband and one for the paramour.
By inference, Rabbi Akiva
is expounding the vavs.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the proof in step 6 was rejected, this brings a new proof that works.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי עקיבא learns from the extra letter ו, not from a repeated word.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי's opposing opinion in the סיפא of the משנה.

steps.title: For רבי עקיבא, six פסוקים are counted
steps.stepSummary: Since every ו counts, the phrase about the waters coming is treated as if it were written six times. The גמרא is about to list them.
steps.simpleTranslation: Therefore, according to רבי עקיבא, six verses are written.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא draws a result from the last step. This line sets up a list that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'ובאו' appears three times in the פרשה, and each time it starts with a ו. רבי עקיבא counts each ו as an extra mention, so three becomes six. Next, the גמרא will show what each one teaches.

keyTerms.meaning: Therefore
Six
Verses (פסוקים)

phrases.english: Therefore, according to Rabbi Akiva,
six verses are written:
phrases.notes: The phrase 'and the waters shall come' appears three times, each with a ו, so it counts as six. The list comes next.

steps.triggerLanguage: הִלְכָּךְ לְרַבִּי עֲקִיבָא שִׁיתָּא קְרָאֵי כְּתִיבִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the conclusion of step 8 (that רבי עקיבא learns from the ו's) to set up a count of the פסוקים.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: For רבי עקיבא, the three mentions of 'ובאו' count as six. This prepares the list of what each one teaches.

steps.title: The six lessons: three for her and three for him
steps.stepSummary: Following רבי עקיבא, each of the three mentions of the waters coming gives two lessons: one about the woman and one about the man. The three topics are the command, the doing, and the knowledge.
steps.simpleTranslation: One is for the command about her, and one is for the command about him. One is for the doing to her, and one is for the doing to him. One is for the knowledge given to her, and one is for the knowledge about him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now gives the list it promised in the last step. Each of the three פסוקים about the waters coming gives two lessons, so we get six in total.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are three פסוקים that talk about the waters coming in, and each one also has an extra ו. The plain words teach a rule about the woman. The extra ו adds the same rule for the man she was with. That is why the six lessons come in three matching pairs.

keyTerms.meaning: Command: the waters are commanded to punish.
Doing: the punishment actually takes effect.
Knowledge: being told what will happen.
Hers, about her (the woman).
His, about him (the man she was with).

steps.confusionAlert: 'His' here does not mean the husband. It means the man the woman is suspected of being with. The waters check him too.

phrases.english: One is for the command concerning her,
phrases.notes: במדבר 5:24. He means God commanding the waters to punish her.

phrases.english: and one is for the command concerning him.
One is for the doing to her,
phrases.notes: במדבר 5:27. This is about the punishment actually happening once she drinks.

phrases.english: and one is for the doing to him.
One is for her knowledge,
phrases.notes: במדבר 5:22. The כהן tells her what the waters will do.

phrases.english: and one is for his knowledge.

steps.triggerLanguage: חַד לְצַוָּאָה דִּידַהּ, וְחַד לְצַוָּאָה דִּידֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Fills in the list of six that step 9 announced.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: According to רבי עקיבא, the three פסוקים plus their extra ו's teach command, doing, and knowledge for both the woman and the man.

steps.title: רבי counts only three, all about the woman
steps.stepSummary: רבי does not learn anything from the extra ו, so for him there are only three פסוקים and three lessons: command, doing, and knowledge.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי holds that three verses are written: one for the command, one for the doing, and one for the knowledge.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains how רבי reads these same פסוקים. Since he does not count the extra ו, he only has three lessons.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This fits step 8, where we saw that רבי does not learn from an extra ו. Without the extra ו's, each פסוק gives one lesson only. So he has command, doing, and knowledge, and nothing extra for the man.

keyTerms.meaning: Three verses.
Are written.

steps.whatToRemember: רבי עקיבא counts the extra ו and gets six lessons, three for her and three for him. רבי does not count it and gets only three, for her.
steps.whyThisMatters: This closes the proof from step 8. The six lessons only work if every ו counts, and רבי's three show exactly where the two opinions part ways.

phrases.english: And according to רבי, three verses are written:
one for the command,
and one for the doing,
and one for the knowledge.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Sets רבי's reading next to רבי עקיבא's six lessons from step 10.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: For רבי, the three פסוקים teach only command, doing, and knowledge, all about the woman.

steps.title: Where does רבי learn that the waters check the man?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for רבי's source that the waters check the man just as they check the woman.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי: the rule that just as the water checks her, it also checks him — where does he learn it from?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a question. רבי does not use the extra ו, so where does he get the rule that the waters check the man too?
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי עקיבא, the man's lessons came from the extra ו's (Step 10). רבי has only three פסוקים and three lessons, all about command, doing and knowledge (Step 11). So he needs a different source for the rule that the waters check the man.

keyTerms.meaning: check, test (the waters test if a person sinned)
her / him
from where does he know it?

phrases.english: And רבי: just as the water checks her
so too it checks him — from where does he learn this?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Since Step 11 showed רבי has no lessons about the man from the ו's, the גמרא asks for his source.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: רבי's source that the waters check the man as well as the woman.

steps.title: A ברייתא: 'the belly and the thigh' means the man's
steps.stepSummary: רבי learns from a ברייתא that 'לצבות בטן ולנפל ירך' speaks about the man, since the woman's belly and thigh are written elsewhere.
steps.simpleTranslation: He learns it from a ברייתא: 'to make the belly swell and the thigh fall' means the belly and thigh of the man. You say it means the man's — maybe it means only the woman's? When the פסוק says 'her belly will swell and her thigh will fall,' the woman's belly and thigh are already stated. So what do I do with 'to make the belly swell and the thigh fall'? It must mean the belly and thigh of the man.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with a ברייתא. One פסוק already talks about the woman's belly and thigh, so the other פסוק must be about the man's.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two פסוקים about belly and thigh. One clearly says 'her' belly and 'her' thigh, so the woman is already covered. The second פסוק would be extra if it were also about her, so the ברייתא uses it for the man.

keyTerms.meaning: the man who was with her
the woman who was with him
belly / thigh
what do I do with (this extra פסוק)?

steps.whyThisMatters: This gives רבי his source for the משנה's rule without needing the extra ו.

phrases.english: He learns it from what was taught in a ברייתא:
'To make the belly swell and the thigh fall' —
phrases.notes: במדבר 5:22

phrases.english: this means the belly and thigh of the man.

phrases.aramaic: אַתָּה אוֹמֵר בִּטְנוֹ וִירֵיכוֹ שֶׁל בּוֹעֵל,
phrases.english: You say it means the belly and thigh of the man,

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ אֵינוֹ אֶלָּא בִּטְנָהּ וִירֵיכָהּ שֶׁל נִבְעֶלֶת?
phrases.english: or maybe it means only the belly and thigh of the woman?
When it says 'and her belly will swell and her thigh will fall,'
phrases.notes: במדבר 5:27

phrases.aramaic: הֲרֵי בִּטְנָהּ וִירֵיכָהּ שֶׁל נִבְעֶלֶת אָמוּר,
phrases.english: the woman's belly and thigh are already stated.

phrases.aramaic: וּמָה אֲנִי מְקַיֵּים ״לַצְבּוֹת בֶּטֶן וְלַנְפִּל יָרֵךְ״ —
phrases.english: So what do I do with 'to make the belly swell and the thigh fall'?
It means the belly and thigh of the man.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 12.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Since פסוק 27 already covers the woman's belly and thigh, פסוק 22 is used for the man's.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא: the כהן tells her the belly comes first
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא uses 'לצבות בטן ולנפל ירך' to teach that the כהן tells her the belly will be hurt first, then the thigh.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the other one (רבי עקיבא): that פסוק teaches that the כהן tells her that the belly comes first and then the thigh, so people won't speak badly about the bitter waters.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains what רבי עקיבא does with the same פסוק. He says it teaches the order: the belly is hurt first, then the thigh.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי עקיבא gets the man's lessons from the extra ו, so he does not need this פסוק for the man. He says this פסוק puts 'belly' before 'thigh' so the כהן can warn her of that order. Then, when it happens that way, no one will say the waters did not work.

keyTerms.meaning: and the other one (the other תנא)
first / and then
bad talk, a bad name
the bitter waters given to the סוטה

phrases.english: And the other one (רבי עקיבא): that פסוק is so the כהן tells her
that the belly comes first and then the thigh,
phrases.notes: In the curse earlier (במדבר 5:21), the thigh comes before the belly, so people could think something went wrong.

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁלֹּא לְהוֹצִיא לַעַז עַל הַמַּיִם הַמָּרִים.
phrases.english: so as not to give the bitter waters a bad name.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After giving רבי's reading of the פסוק, the גמרא explains how רבי עקיבא uses that same פסוק.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי עקיבא uses the פסוק to teach that the כהן tells her the belly is hurt before the thigh.

steps.title: רבי: the wording 'belly' and 'thigh' points to the man
steps.stepSummary: רבי rejects רבי עקיבא's reading: if the פסוק were about the woman, it would say 'her belly' and 'her thigh.'
steps.simpleTranslation: And the other one (רבי): if so, the פסוק should have written 'her belly and her thigh.' Why does it say just 'belly' and 'thigh'? Learn from this that it is about the man.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי explains why he does not read the פסוק like רבי עקיבא. The words do not say 'her,' so they must mean the man.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי focuses on the exact wording. A פסוק about the woman would say 'her belly, her thigh,' like פסוק 27 does. Since פסוק 22 says only 'belly' and 'thigh,' רבי says it means the man.

keyTerms.meaning: if so
the פסוק should have written
learn from this

steps.whatToRemember: רבי: 'לצבות בטן ולנפל ירך' means the man, because פסוק 27 already covers the woman and this פסוק does not say 'her.' רבי עקיבא: it teaches that the belly is hurt before the thigh, so no one gives the waters a bad name.

phrases.english: And the other one (רבי): if so,
the פסוק should have written 'her belly and her thigh.'
Why does it say just 'belly' and 'thigh'?
Learn from this that it is about the man.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: רבי responds to רבי עקיבא's reading from Step 14.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects רבי עקיבא's reading that the פסוק is about the woman.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: If the פסוק were about the woman it would say 'her belly' and 'her thigh'; the missing 'her' shows it is about the man.

steps.title: Maybe the whole verse is only about the man
steps.stepSummary: Working inside רבי's view, the גמרא asks: maybe the entire phrase 'לצבות בטן ולנפל ירך' only teaches that the waters check the man, and teaches nothing about the order of the punishment.
steps.simpleTranslation: But say that the whole phrase comes only for this purpose: to teach about the man.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back. It asks: maybe the whole phrase is only about the man, like רבי said, and it does not teach anything about the order of the punishment at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 15 showed that the words do not say 'her belly' and 'her thigh'. So it seems the phrase is not about the woman. If that is true, maybe רבי עקיבא's lesson about the order (belly first, then thigh) has no place in this פסוק.

keyTerms.meaning: And say / maybe you could say (opens a challenge)
All of it, the whole thing
It comes for this purpose

phrases.english: But say that all of it
phrases.notes: Some versions leave out the word in round brackets. The word in square brackets is the corrected wording.

phrases.english: comes for this purpose?
phrases.notes: 'This' means teaching that the waters check the man too.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on רבי's point in Step 15 and asks whether, for רבי, the whole phrase is used up on the man, so that the order lesson from Step 14 has no source.
steps.kashyaTarget: The assumption that, even according to רבי, 'לצבות בטן ולנפל ירך' still teaches the order of the punishment (belly first, then thigh).
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the words are not about the woman, the whole phrase could be used only for the man. Then nothing is left over to teach the order.

steps.title: The general wording teaches two lessons
steps.stepSummary: If the phrase were only about the man, it would say 'his belly' and 'his thigh'. Since it says just 'belly' and 'thigh', we learn two things from it.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, the תורה should have written 'his belly' and 'his thigh'. Why does it say just 'belly' and 'thigh'? Learn two things from it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge with the same kind of logic רבי used. Since the תורה wrote neither 'her' nor 'his', the phrase covers both lessons.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי argued that the phrase cannot be only about the woman, because it does not say 'her'. The same argument works the other way: it cannot be only about the man, because it does not say 'his'. So the general words teach two things: the man is checked, and the כהן tells the woman the order of the punishment.

keyTerms.meaning: If so
Let it write / it should have written
His belly and his thigh
Learn two things from it

steps.whatToRemember: The general words 'בטן' and 'ירך' (not 'her' and not 'his') teach two lessons: the waters check the man, and the כהן warns her that the belly is hurt first and then the thigh.

phrases.english: If so, let it write 'his belly' and 'his thigh.'
Why does it say just 'belly' and 'thigh'?
Learn two things from it.
phrases.notes: The two things are that the man is checked too, and that the כהן tells her the order of the punishment.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 16's challenge.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Wording analysis: the general wording includes both readings
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The phrase is only about the man.
steps.terutzMaskana: Because it says neither 'his' nor 'her', the phrase teaches both lessons.

steps.title: Back to the משנה: רבי יהושע quotes זכריה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא returns to the next line of the משנה, where רבי יהושע says this was how זכריה used to explain the פסוק.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהושע said: This is how זכריה used to explain it, and so on.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next part of the משנה to begin discussing it. This line sets up the next discussion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה, רבי יהושע says this about רבי עקיבא's teaching just before it, that the wife is forbidden to both the בעל and the בועל from 'נטמאה ונטמאה'. זכריה בן הקצב taught the same thing. רבי's view about the two mentions of 'נטמאה' is a separate opinion that comes right after in the משנה. The ברייתא that comes next counts a third mention of 'נטמאה' and a third prohibition.

keyTerms.meaning: Explains or learns a lesson from a פסוק
And so on (the rest of the quote is assumed)

phrases.english: רבי יהושע said:
This is how זכריה used to explain it, and so on.
phrases.notes: This is quoted from our משנה. רבי יהושע is saying that זכריה בן הקצב taught the same thing as רבי עקיבא's teaching just before it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ: כָּךְ הָיָה דּוֹרֵשׁ זְכַרְיָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on from the 'belly and thigh' discussion to the next line of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Opens the discussion of the משנה line about how many times 'נטמאה' is written and what each one teaches.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא: three mentions of 'defiled' teach three prohibitions
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that 'נטמאה' is written three times in the סוטה section. רבי עקיבא says each one teaches a prohibition: to her husband, to the other man, and from eating תרומה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: The word 'defiled' is said three times in the section: 'if she is defiled', 'she is defiled', and 'and is defiled'. Why? One forbids her to her husband, one forbids her to the other man, and one forbids her from eating תרומה. These are the words of רבי עקיבא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא. In it, רבי עקיבא counts three mentions of 'נטמאה' and gives each one its own lesson.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי, in the משנה, counted two mentions and got two prohibitions. רבי עקיבא counts three and adds a third prohibition: she may not eat תרומה, even if she is the wife or daughter of a כהן.

keyTerms.meaning: She became defiled (forbidden)
Husband
The other man she was secluded with
The holy portion of produce that only כהנים and their families may eat

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
The three times that are said in the section
'if she is defiled,' 'she is defiled,' and 'and is defiled': why are they needed?
One is for the husband, and one is for the other man,
and one is for תרומה,
These are the words of רבי עקיבא.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: שָׁלֹשׁ פְּעָמִים הָאֲמוּרִין בַּפָּרָשָׁה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a ברייתא on the topic raised by the משנה line in Step 18.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The three mentions of 'נטמאה' forbid the סוטה to her husband, to the other man, and from eating תרומה.

steps.title: רבי ישמעאל: a קל וחומר forbids her to a כהן
steps.stepSummary: רבי ישמעאל argues with a קל וחומר. A divorced woman is allowed to eat תרומה but still may not marry a כהן. So a סוטה, who may not even eat תרומה, should surely be forbidden to marry a כהן.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ישמעאל said: It is a קל וחומר. A divorced woman is allowed to eat תרומה, yet she is forbidden to marry a כהן. This woman is forbidden to eat תרומה, so is it not logical that she is forbidden to marry a כהן?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי ישמעאל adds another prohibition for the סוטה, that she may not marry a כהן. He learns it through logic, without needing a פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The קל וחומר goes from the lighter case to the stricter one. A גרושה has a milder status, since she may eat תרומה, and she is still forbidden to a כהן. The סוטה has a stricter status, since she may not eat תרומה, so she should surely be forbidden to a כהן as well.

keyTerms.meaning: A logical argument from a lighter case to a stricter one
A divorced woman
The priesthood; here, marrying a כהן
Is it not logical?

steps.confusionAlert: The גרושה here is a כהן's daughter who was divorced. She may go back to eat תרומה in her father's house, but a כהן still may not marry any divorced woman.

phrases.english: רבי ישמעאל said: It is a קל וחומר:
If a divorced woman, who is allowed to eat תרומה,
phrases.notes: This is a כהן's daughter who was divorced and has no children. She goes back to eating תרומה at her father's house (ויקרא 22:13).

phrases.english: is forbidden to marry a כהן,
phrases.notes: ויקרא 21:7

phrases.english: then this one, who is forbidden to eat תרומה,
is it not logical that she is forbidden to marry a כהן?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds to רבי עקיבא's list in the same ברייתא. It uses logic to forbid the סוטה from marrying a כהן.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Through a קל וחומר from a גרושה, the סוטה is forbidden to marry a כהן.

steps.title: A woman in doubt is still forbidden
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא points to a strange double phrase in the פסוק and learns from it that a סוטה whose status is a ספק is forbidden to her husband.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why does the verse say both 'and she was defiled' and 'and she was not defiled'? If she was defiled, why does she drink? If she was not defiled, why does he make her drink? The verse is telling you that even when it is uncertain, she is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא continues to explain the סוטה section. It points out that the פסוק describes her both as defiled and as not defiled, and it learns from this that a woman in doubt is still forbidden.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If we knew for sure that she sinned, she would not need the water test. If we knew for sure that she did not sin, there would be no reason for the test either. So the פסוק must be talking about a ספק, and the תורה still treats her as forbidden to her husband until the water settles the question.

keyTerms.meaning: Why does the verse say this? What does it come to teach?
She was defiled. Here it means she was with another man.
He makes her drink the bitter water.
A case where we do not know what happened
The verse is telling you

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up a key idea: by סוטה, a ספק is treated like a ודאי. The next step builds a קל וחומר on exactly this point.

phrases.english: What does the verse come to teach when it says
'and she was defiled' and 'and she was not defiled'?
phrases.notes: במדבר 5:14

phrases.english: If she was defiled, why does she drink?
If she was not defiled, why does he make her drink?
The verse is telling you
that when it is uncertain, she is forbidden.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The ברייתא moves from the three times נטמאה is written to another lesson from the same פסוק.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A סוטה whose sin is only a ספק is still forbidden to her husband.

steps.title: Building a קל וחומר from סוטה to שרץ
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא starts a קל וחומר. סוטה is lenient about accidental cases, yet it treats a ספק like a ודאי. שרץ is strict about accidental cases, so it should surely treat a ספק like a ודאי.
steps.simpleTranslation: From here you can learn about a שרץ. סוטה is a case where the תורה did not treat an accident like a deliberate act, or force like willing consent, and still it treated a doubtful case like a certain one. שרץ is a case where the תורה did treat an accident like a deliberate act, and force like willing consent. Is it not logical that it should treat a doubtful case...
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא takes the lesson from סוטה, that a ספק counts like a ודאי, and begins to apply it to טומאת שרץ through a קל וחומר. The sentence finishes on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By סוטה, a woman who sinned by accident or by force is not forbidden. That makes סוטה the more lenient case, and even so a ספק is treated as forbidden. By שרץ, a person becomes טמא even by accident or against his will, so it is the stricter case, and a ספק should surely count as טמא.

keyTerms.meaning: From here you can learn
A creeping creature whose dead body makes things טמא
An accidental act treated like a deliberate one
Being forced treated like doing it willingly
A doubtful case treated like a certain one
Is it not logical? This is the opening of a קל וחומר.

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two kinds of leniency. 'שוגג כמזיד' is about how the act happened, accident or on purpose. 'ספק כודאי' is about what we know, whether it happened at all. The קל וחומר uses strictness in the first to argue for strictness in the second.
steps.whyThisMatters: This begins a source for treating a ספק טומאה as טמא, and the rule is learned from סוטה.

phrases.english: From here you can learn about a שרץ:
If by סוטה, where the תורה did not make
an accident like a deliberate act, or being forced like doing it willingly,
phrases.notes: A woman who sinned by accident or was forced is not forbidden to her husband.

phrases.english: it still made a doubtful case like a certain one,
then by a שרץ, where it did make
an accident like a deliberate act, and being forced like doing it willingly,
phrases.notes: You become טמא from a שרץ even if you touched it by accident or against your will.

phrases.english: is it not logical that it should make a doubtful case
phrases.notes: The sentence finishes on the next amud: 'like a certain one.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: It takes the rule from step 21, that a ספק סוטה is forbidden, and starts to extend it by קל וחומר to ספק טומאת שרץ.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Through a קל וחומר from סוטה, a ספק טומאה from a שרץ should be treated like a certain case. The conclusion continues on the next amud.
